poeticComment: The world is overwhelmingly green and alive.
Long, lazy afternoons are spent in the shade of the great tree.
The river flows low and clear, revealing the smooth stones of its bed.
The heat makes the distant cliffs shimmer.
A distant thunderstorm rumbles, but never arrives.
The scent of hot rock and dry grass fills the air.
The sun beats down, bleaching the stones white.
Life is easy, the world is full of food and light.
Berries ripen in the thickets, a treasure of sweetness.
Dust rises from the game trails.
The air hums with the drone of bees.
The nights are short and filled with the sound of insects.
The earth is cracked and dry in the open plains.
The world seems to slow down under the weight of the heat.
The days are long and golden.
The children splash in the cool water of the river bend.
A hawk circles lazily in the vast, blue sky.
Lizards dart across sun-warmed stones.
Shadows are short and sharp at midday.
The air is heavy with the scent of pine and salt.

Survival is a quiet, constant effort.
Time seems to slow, measured in logs for the fire.
The stored food is a promise of life through the darkness.
The only sound is the wind whistling through the rocks.
A weak sun offers no warmth.
The silence of the snow-covered land is absolute.
Icicles hang like fangs from the cave mouth.
Every venture from the shelter is a calculated risk.
The world seems to hold its breath under a blanket of snow.
